title: MediSafe_controversy
summary:
The MediSafe controversy refers to a public debate that emerged in Hong Kong between June and September 2025 after questions arose about the originality and data practices of MediSafe, a purportedly student-built artificial intelligence platform. In April 2024, MediSafe won the Student Innovation Grand Award at the Hong Kong ICT Awards, and in April 2025 the project received a Silver Medal at the International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva.

On 13 June 2025, Hailey Cheng Hei Lam raised concerns publicly on Threads. Some users pointed out that the MediSafe website previously redirected to AI Health Studio, a U.S.-based software company. The company's wording was later changed, with what was originally described as "developed" becoming "optimised" and "commercialised." On 5 August 2025, Ahmed Jemaa, co-founder of AI Health Studio, issued an official statement clarifying that the company had not been informed the application they developed would be submitted to academic competitions, maintaining this gave unfair advantage to other student participants. Jemaa emphasised that AI Health Studio developed the minimum viable product entirely independently.

On 27 August, St. Paul's Co-educational College issued a public statement that the school had no prior knowledge of AI Health Studio's involvement in the project. The Digital Policy Office said it had requested a full investigation by Hong Kong Education City and the Hong Kong ICT Awards' Quality Assurance Panel. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data confirmed it had received a complaint and was reviewing the matter. On 22 August 2025, the parents of Poon announced that they would voluntarily return all the awards MediSafe won.

In a significant twist, Hailey Cheng, the City University student who originally raised concerns, was arrested in February 2026 for allegedly disclosing somebody's personal data without their consent and causing them harm.
